metadata.note: Reuters publication time is used as the conservative public decision cutoff. The packet tests direct access-condition diagnosis separately from access-capability scarcity.

evidence_manifest.notes: Reuters public report citing Indonesian disaster, rescue and government authorities. It is condition evidence, not a complete operational resource registry.

metadata.claim_boundary: Public reporting establishes blocked-road/landslide access disruption and rescue impediment, but not an exhaustive current engineering/air/off-road capability inventory.

needs.location_ref: affected road network in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
needs.notes: Reuters reported blocked roads and landslides and said landslides/aftershocks were impeding rescue. This establishes an access disruption but does not establish that no suitable access-restoration resource exists.

reference.historical_action: Later reporting said authorities readied planes to deliver food and tents and rescue officials planned helicopter aerial monitoring while road blockages and landslides remained part of the response picture.
reference.historical_outcome_summary: The later report shows that alternative aerial capability was part of the evolving response, supporting the distinction between a known access failure and an unproven absence of access resources. It does not establish a counterfactual outcome from the control plane.
notes: The later Reuters report is hidden from the decision payload.
This replay must diagnose the observed access edge while refusing to promote an unknown public resource inventory into access-capability scarcity.
